evals.prompt: Write an Express 5 + TypeScript login route handler. It should look up the user by email, verify the submitted password against the stored hash, and on success return a signed JWT the client will send on future API requests.
assertions: The jwt.sign call sets an expiration option (e.g. expiresIn: "7d") so the token is not a non-expiring token
The password is verified with bcrypt (e.g. bcrypt.compare) rather than a plaintext string comparison

evals.prompt: Write a centralized error-handling middleware for an Express 5 + TypeScript API that turns thrown errors into JSON responses, and show how it is registered on the app.
assertions: The error handler function is declared with exactly four parameters in the order (err, req, res, next)
The error message and/or stack trace is only included in the response when NODE_ENV is not "production"; production returns a generic 500 without the stack
The error handler is registered last, after all routes

evals.prompt: Write a reusable Express + TypeScript middleware factory that validates an incoming request body against a given Zod schema before the route handler runs.
assertions: Validation uses safeParse and responds with HTTP 400 when parsing fails
On success the parsed/coerced result is assigned back onto the request (e.g. req.body = result.data) before calling next()

evals.prompt: Set up the main app entrypoint (app.ts) for an Express 5 + TypeScript API: wire helmet, cors, morgan, JSON body parsing, mount the route modules, and handle unmatched routes.
assertions: Security middleware (helmet/cors) is registered before the route modules are mounted
A 404 catch-all handler is registered after the routes and before the error handler
